headline: CPI runs hot — the October hike is back in play: DXY to an 18-month high, October a coin flip at ~43–47%; Beige Book and Goolsbee confirm the hawkish read into Thursday's PPI.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: Hot core broke the October-hold thesis: October 27–28 went from ~23% priced to a coin flip (~43–47%), December is effectively fully priced, and DXY printed a new 18-month high — the $35.5bn of crowded longs got paid, not squeezed.
chapters.meaning: What changed: September CPI ran hot on the measures the Fed actually trades — headline 3.7% y/y (vs 3.6% expected) on +0.6% m/m, but core is the number and it beat twice: 0.3% m/m vs 0.2% expected, 2.6% y/y vs 2.5%. Gasoline's +9.1% drove over half the monthly gain, yet the broadening is what repriced the Fed — shelter +0.4%, and services running hot with ‘little sign of improvement,’ in Goolsbee's words. The market repriced in minutes: the 2-year jumped 7bp to 4.872% almost immediately (13bp on the session to 4.92%), the 10-year added ~5–11bp to ~5.29%, and October 27–28 hike odds roughly doubled from ~22–23% to a coin flip (~43–47%). DXY broke to a new 18-month high (~102.75) and, crucially, held the bid through the afternoon (~102.9) instead of fading it. The afternoon then confirmed the morning: the 1pm CT Beige Book ran hot-leaning — three districts reporting ‘robust’ price growth, four saying the pace picked up, ‘higher oil prices permeated all District reports’ — and Goolsbee's 2pm CT Yahoo Finance interview called the print ‘discouraging’ and reaffirmed the 2% target. Barkin's 12:30pm remarks never surfaced in the wires. Thread: this morning the thesis was the hawkish hold in its sixth week — October shelved at ~77% hold, December ~84%, and $35.5bn of dollar longs crowded into a single print with the squeeze risk on a soft number. What it means: breaks the morning thesis outright. The ‘one more hike, but in December’ framing shifts to ‘possibly October’ — fork 1 of the morning's Focus preview is the one that played out. The positioning read inverts too: the crowded longs were rewarded, so the unwind risk now sits on the other side — a soft PPI tomorrow would hurt far more than it would have yesterday. And note the calendar quirk that hardens the hawkish path: September PCE, the Fed's preferred gauge, doesn't print until October 29, after the meeting — so the 27–28 decision gets made on CPI, tomorrow's PPI, and jobs, not on PCE.
chapters.fx: What to watch: PPI + retail sales + jobless claims Thursday 7:30am CT — PPI is the next inflation read and the last big one before the blackout starts Saturday Oct 17. Warsh speaks Thursday 10:30pm CT. For the pair legs: Japan machinery orders tonight 6:50pm CT, UK data dump Thursday 1:00am CT, Australia jobs Thursday 7:30pm CT.

scenarios.base: October stays a coin flip into PPI; DXY consolidates the 18-month-high break around 102.5–103.5.
scenarios.bear: Soft PPI and soft retail sales walk back the October repricing — the crowded longs unwind and DXY gives back the break.
scenarios.bull: Hot PPI confirms the broadening — October gets fully priced and the dollar extends the breakout.

numbers: DXY ~102.9 — new 18-mo high ~102.75 post-print, bid held all session

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The dollar leg knocked EUR/USD from 1.1208 to 1.1134 (-0.6%) on the print; it steadied near 1.1155 into the close — but the euro's own story firmed at the margin, with hot German wholesale prices keeping the ECB's December hike case alive.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the pair fell with the dollar leg, not on euro news — 1.1208 pre-print to ~1.1134 after (-0.6%), steadying around 1.1155 (-0.39% on the day) into the New York close. The euro's own data actually leaned hawkish: German wholesale prices ran +8.7% y/y (m/m 1.9% vs 0.6% expected) — the hottest since February 2023, on mineral-oil prices — which firms the ECB's December-hike case even as October stays ~12%. Germany's 30-year auction held at 3.8%, unchanged — steady absorption, no duration-fear escalation. On the fiscal front, France's budget cleared its first hurdle: the Socialist rejection motion failed 236–149, though the revenue vote (Oct 20) and Moody's review (Oct 23) are still ahead. Thread: the morning had the euro stabilizing off the 17-month low on dollar softness and record-bearish specs (net shorts -99,332, ~0th percentile), with Lagarde keeping December alive (‘cannot wait until in full view’) while putting France's debt on Paris. What it means: confirms the shape, breaks the level. The morning's 1.1150–1.1250 grind broke below on the dollar leg — the euro's own drivers improved at the margin (hotter pipeline inflation, a cleared French hurdle) but the Fed-ECB gap widened against it as October revived. The record-bearish EUR positioning got paid today too; the squeeze setup is still loaded, just denied its trigger.
chapters.fx: What to watch: EU summit Thursday (fiscal burden-sharing, energy security — headline risk for EUR); French revenue vote Oct 20; Moody's Oct 23; US PPI Thursday 7:30am CT for the dollar leg of the pair.

scenarios.base: EUR/USD consolidates 1.11–1.12; the dollar leg decides, the ECB leg steadies.
scenarios.bear: Hot PPI extends the October repricing — 1.11 gives way and the 17-month low comes back into view.
scenarios.bull: Soft PPI unwinds the dollar bid and the record EUR shorts squeeze — 1.1250+ in a hurry.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: Cable took the dollar leg lower with the rest (1.3256 → ~1.319) — but sterling's own story didn't change: Bailey added nothing overnight, and the ~86% November hike case carries into Thursday's GDP print.
chapters.meaning: What changed: only the dollar leg — GBP/USD slid from the morning's 1.3256 toward ~1.319 on the post-CPI dollar bid, holding above the 1.3140–60 support zone. Nothing sterling-specific moved: Bailey's overnight remarks added nothing new, and the November 5 hike case sits ~86% priced. Thread: sterling remains the best of the European losers, floored by the BoE's hawkish hold while the euro handles its fiscal drama. What it means: thesis stands — a quiet currency is not a chapter. Thursday's 1:00am CT data dump (GDP fcst -0.1% m/m) is the growth counterpoint that can move the hike case.
chapters.fx: What to watch: UK data dump Thursday 1:00am CT — GDP m/m fcst -0.1%; Bailey speaks again Thursday; US PPI Thursday 7:30am CT for the dollar leg.

scenarios.base: Cable drifts with the dollar into Thursday's data.
scenarios.bear: Weak UK GDP dents the hike case — cable slips toward 1.3140 support.
scenarios.bull: Soft US PPI knocks the dollar leg out — cable reclaims 1.3250+.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: USD/JPY rode the US yield leg from ~158.2 to ~158.84 (+0.3%) as the October-hike repricing widened the rate gap further in the dollar's favor — the morning's hot-CPI bull scenario, playing out.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the pair did exactly what the morning's bull scenario sketched — hot core revived October-hike talk and USD/JPY climbed ~158.2 → ~158.84 (+0.3%) on the 2-year's 13bp jump. The BoJ side didn't move: the ‘December, not October’ shape stands (October ~9%, December >80%), with the source report leaning against back-to-back hikes. Thread: the pair has breathed with the US yield leg for three straight sessions; the gap is the engine and the engine just got bigger. What it means: confirms and extends. The rate gap favoring the dollar widened — negative for the yen by the scoring rule — and the only yen-side offset is tonight's core machinery orders (6:50pm CT), which rarely moves the pair. The intervention-watch level creeps closer, but there is no sign of it.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Japan core machinery orders tonight 6:50pm CT; US PPI Thursday — the pair's only real engine remains the US yield leg; BoJ Oct 29–30.

scenarios.base: USD/JPY consolidates 158–159.5; the gap pulls, the BoJ's December lean caps the pace.
scenarios.bear: Soft PPI collapses the October repricing — the pair slips back under 157.5.
scenarios.bull: Hot PPI fully prices October — 159.5+ and the intervention chatter starts.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The haven still hasn't bid — the franc slept through CPI day too, with fear continuing to express through crude instead of currencies.
chapters.meaning: What changed: nothing verifiable — no fresh USD/CHF quote surfaced and Schlegel's remarks (11:30pm CT tonight) are still ahead. Thread: the franc has slept through a week of escalation; fear keeps expressing through crude, not currencies. What it means: the haven race still hasn't started. Hot CPI moved the dollar on rates, not fear — the franc only moves on a verified shock or a verified de-escalation.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Schlegel tonight 11:30pm CT; any verified Hormuz/Saudi development; EUR/CHF as the contagion gauge.

scenarios.base: The franc drifts with the dollar's tide.
scenarios.bear: Verified de-escalation — the fear premium clears.
scenarios.bull: A verified supply shock — the haven bid finally finds the franc.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The $0.70 test failed — hot US CPI killed the squeeze the morning was waiting on; the Aussie slipped back to ~0.697 on the dollar leg while China's export boom held a floor, not a bid.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the squeeze setup died at the trigger. AUD/USD had knocked on $0.70 overnight (0.6978–0.7004) on China's +36.3% export boom — then hot US CPI reasserted the dollar leg and the Aussie slipped back to ~0.6971, ending the day lower. China's own data stayed mixed in the rearview: exports +36.3% (AI hardware, fastest since February), CPI soft at 0.9%, PPI hot at 5.0% on oil. Thread: the RBA's tightening bias is intact (unanimous minutes, waiting ‘could be costly’), specs are short Aussies at the ~2nd percentile with record gross shorts, and the morning's read was that a soft CPI fires the squeeze. What it means: breaks the morning's bull path — the trigger went the other way. The positioning is still a loaded spring (stretched shorts = squeeze potential by the rule), but it needs a new catalyst; Thursday's Australia jobs (7:30pm CT, fcst 19.6K, unemployment 4.6%) is the next domestic one.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Australia jobs Thursday 7:30pm CT (fcst 19.6K, unemp 4.6%); US PPI Thursday 7:30am CT — the dollar leg still decides; RBA Nov 2–3.

scenarios.base: AUD chops under 0.698; the China beat holds the floor.
scenarios.bear: Hot PPI extends the dollar bid — 0.69 gives way.
scenarios.bull: Soft PPI revives the squeeze on record shorts — $0.70 gets retested.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The 161bp rate gap won again — hot US CPI repriced the Fed leg wider and USD/CAD pressed toward the 52-week high, with only oil's held bid (WTI ~$95) keeping the loonie from breaking it.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the tug-of-war tilted to the gap. USD/CAD rose ~45 pips on the day as the hot print repriced the Fed leg of the 161bp US-Canada 2-year gap wider — the pair pressed toward the 52-week high of 1.4299. The offset held but didn't advance: WTI ~$95 and Brent ~$106 kept crude's tailwind in place after the Aramco-building confirmation and the two confirmed Hormuz vessel strikes, and Canada's building permits beat big (+8.8% vs 2.9% expected) — but permits are texture against the -68.3K jobs shock, not a game-changer. Thread: the -68.3K jobs print broke the hawkish-BoC thesis; the gap has won every tug-of-war since, with oil thickening the loonie's defense. What it means: confirms the thesis — the gap decides, oil cushions. October 28 BoC hike pricing (~25%) has no reason to move on today's data; Thursday's US PPI is the gap's next examiner, and Canada's manufacturing sales print alongside it.
chapters.fx: What to watch: US PPI + Canada manufacturing sales Thursday 7:30am CT; the 1.4299 52-week high — a break opens 1.44; BoC Oct 28.

scenarios.base: USD/CAD grinds against 1.43; oil cushions, the gap pulls.
scenarios.bear: Hot PPI widens the gap further — the 52-week high breaks toward 1.44.
scenarios.bull: Soft PPI narrows the gap — the oil offset finally bites and the loonie firms back toward 1.41.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: The kiwi took the dollar leg lower and hovers just above its 52-week low — nothing of its own changed; the RBNZ's October 28 two-way bet remains the only thing on the calendar.
chapters.meaning: What changed: only the dollar leg — NZD/USD slid ~44 pips with the post-CPI bid and hovers just above its 52-week low (0.5580). China's export beat kept it off the low but gave it nothing more. Thread: the RBNZ sits at 2.75% with October 28 a genuine two-way bet (~50% priced); NZ CPI lands Oct 21 and settles it. What it means: thesis stands — the kiwi drifts with risk sentiment and the dollar into the RBNZ.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Crude held the re-bid through CPI day: Brent ~$106, WTI ~$95, spread ~$11 — two confirmed Hormuz vessel strikes (one sunk) and the Aramco-building confirmation kept the shipping premium bid while OPEC cut demand growth for a sixth straight month.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the premium held rather than leaked. Brent ~$106.06, WTI ~$95.09 into the New York afternoon — the Aramco administrative-building strike confirmation (Houthi claim, Riyadh confirmed, limited fire) plus two confirmed Hormuz vessel strikes on Wednesday (MPA: two Singapore-flagged ships struck, GFS Pride sank) kept the shipping-risk premium bid for a third day. The coalition's Tuesday strikes on Houthi fuel sites in Sanaa and the Houthis' vow of more attacks on Saudi airports and oil facilities kept the escalation tape running. OPEC's monthly: 2026 demand growth cut to ~180k bpd — a sixth straight cut — while 2027 was lifted to 2.55M on inventory rebuilding. The Brent-WTI spread sits ~$11 (normal $3–5) — still shipping risk and geopolitics, not demand. Thread: Monday the market bought the war back, Tuesday it faded the premium on the Russian diesel story, overnight the Aramco confirmation re-bid it — Wednesday confirmed the ‘negotiable premium’ read: each verified hit re-bids, each diesel headline leaks. What it means: confirms the range thesis — Brent $104–108 holds until a verified supply shock or a verified ceasefire breaks it. For FX: crude's held bid keeps the tailwind under CAD and the tax on JPY/EUR.
chapters.fx: What to watch: whether the Aramco hit draws a Saudi response; Trump's Saturday Hormuz deadline; physical diesel cargoes — the deal's real test. Spread toward $15 = Hormuz risk back in force; toward $5 = premium truly unwinding.

scenarios.base: Brent holds $104–108; the market needs a verified shock or ceasefire to leave the range.
scenarios.bear: Ceasefire confirmation or fast restarts — Brent under $100, spread collapses toward $5.
scenarios.bull: Verified Hormuz disruption or Saudi retaliation — Brent toward $110+, spread past $15.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Hot CPI armed both of gold's engines at once — and the rate leg won: the metal slid to ~$4,094 (-1.4%) as the 2-year's 13bp surge lifted real yields, capping the anti-dollar bid.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the both-engines moment arrived and split against gold. September CPI's hot core (0.3% m/m, 2.6% y/y) revived the October hike — the 2-year surged 13bp to 4.92%, the 10-year to ~5.29% — and the rate leg overpowered the dollar leg: spot slid from ~$4,150 to ~$4,094 (-1.4%) into the New York afternoon. Silver fell harder (-3.2% to $57.39), the classic risk-off tell. Thread: Tuesday's read was that the dollar leg alone wasn't enough with real yields capped; the morning said CPI arms both engines at once. What it means: confirms the two-engine model — the anti-dollar tell needs the rate leg cooperating, and today it didn't. The morning's map holds: hot core sent gold back toward $4,000; only a soft PPI re-arms it toward $4,300.
chapters.fx: What to watch: US PPI Thursday 7:30am CT — the next both-engines moment; real yields (2Y 4.92%) are the cap to watch.

scenarios.base: Gold consolidates under the rate cap; direction comes from PPI.
scenarios.bear: Hot PPI fully prices October — real yields jump again and gold slides toward $4,000.
scenarios.bull: Soft PPI collapses the October repricing — gold re-arms toward $4,300 and the anti-dollar trade broadens.
